stories.head: Adobe acquires Rilo to add AI workflow orchestration to enterprise marketing
stories.plain: Adobe is buying Rilo, a tool that orchestrates AI workflows around enterprise marketing tasks. This matters because it signals Adobe is moving beyond content generation into automating the surrounding work — briefing, approvals, distribution — which reshapes how marketing teams will buy and build AI tooling at scale.

stories.head: GEO is now a weekly job as AI answers shift constantly
stories.plain: Because ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini reshuffle which sources they cite week to week, Generative Engine Optimization can no longer be a one-off project. PR, SEO, and content teams need a shared, recurring process to track what buyers ask and which answers get surfaced — a practical governance shift for most marketing orgs.

stories.head: Videowise launches AI Visibility suite to get UGC cited inside AI search answers
stories.plain: Videowise converts TikTok and Instagram videos into structured, machine-readable content that AI engines like ChatGPT and Gemini can cite. For Shopify brands, this is a direct product bet that social UGC — not just text — can win placement in AI-generated answers, making GEO a visual-content problem for the first time.

stories.head: Globant launches MuleSoft AI Pod to speed enterprise agentic AI integration with Salesforce
stories.plain: Globant's new delivery model pairs specialized AI agents with human integration experts to cut API migration timelines from months to weeks inside Salesforce environments. It matters because slow integration has been the main bottleneck for enterprises trying to deploy agentic AI at scale, and this is a direct commercial answer to that problem.

stories.head: Contentful study: 350 marketing leaders flag five urgent questions for agentic AI integration
stories.plain: A survey of 350 marketing decision-makers by Atlantic Re:think and Contentful identifies five governance gaps that leaders must resolve before agentic AI can run reliably in enterprise marketing. The findings give practitioners a concrete checklist for where policy, data, and oversight need to catch up with technology.

stories.head: The terrifying loophole in your autonomous tech stack
stories.plain: When AI agents hand data to each other to run campaigns, each handoff is a potential leak of customer or proprietary data. This piece maps the data-passing vulnerabilities in agentic stacks and explains the controls marketers need before they hand agents real authority. Essential reading for anyone deploying or buying autonomous marketing systems.

stories.head: Rapid AI changes mean GEO is a weekly job now
stories.plain: AI answer engines update their citation logic so fast that Generative Engine Optimization can't be a quarterly project anymore. The article argues that PR, SEO, and content teams need a shared weekly workflow tracking what buyers ask, which sources get cited, and what shifts. Practical operational guidance for brands trying to stay visible inside AI answers.

stories.head: Marketers know AI is using bad data to make decisions
stories.plain: Survey data shows marketers are granting AI more decision-making authority even while acknowledging their CRM data is dirty and unreliable. Flawed inputs corrupt revenue measurement, attribution, and every AI decision downstream. This matters because it reframes data quality from a hygiene issue into a core AI governance risk.

stories.head: The latest AI-powered martech news: Adobe acquires Rilo for AI workflow orchestration
stories.plain: Adobe's acquisition of Rilo adds AI workflow orchestration to its enterprise marketing suite, signalling that the big platforms are buying orchestration capability rather than building it. This shifts how enterprise marketing AI is assembled and bought, making it a meaningful structural move for the martech stack.

stories.head: Videowise launches AI Visibility to make UGC visible to generative AI engines
stories.plain: Videowise is turning TikTok and Instagram UGC into structured, schema-rich content that ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini can cite. It's the first GEO product aimed specifically at video commerce brands on Shopify. Signals a fast-growing category where social proof content must be engineered for AI answer engines, not just search crawlers.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: GEO & AI Brand Visibility Become a Weekly Discipline
body: As AI engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity become primary discovery surfaces, generative engine optimization (GEO) is no longer a quarterly SEO task — it requires constant attention because AI models update their knowledge and ranking signals far faster than Google ever did. Brands that treated search optimization as a slow, set-and-forget discipline are finding themselves invisible to AI-generated answers almost overnight.

The practical shift is that marketers must now engineer content specifically so AI systems can find, trust, and cite their brand — covering structured data, authoritative sourcing, and real-time monitoring. Tools like Videowise's AI Visibility launch signal that an entire product category is forming around this need, turning AI discoverability into a standing line item in the marketing budget.

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves from Hype to Integration Stack
body: Multiple enterprise announcements this month — Globant's MuleSoft AI Pod, Workato-Lenovo's Qira expansion, and Adobe's MCP app inside Slack — share a common logic: AI agents only create value when they can act across systems without human hand-offs. The bottleneck is no longer model capability but integration plumbing, and vendors are racing to own that connective layer.

The Contentful report on the 'Agentic Web' frames the executive-level question clearly: who controls the agent, who audits what it does, and what happens when it touches customer data across a fifteen-tool stack? Choosing an agent orchestration layer is now a strategic governance decision, not a developer experiment, and organizations that delay the governance conversation are accumulating silent risk.
ev: MarTech Series · Globant MuleSoft AI Pod

themes.head: AI Governance & the Autonomous Stack Loophole
body: Three separate pieces this month converge on an uncomfortable truth: most marketing AI stacks have no meaningful governance layer. Marketers openly admit AI is acting on bad or incomplete data, autonomous tools can execute decisions no human explicitly approved, and the governance tests that matter most are the ones teams haven't run yet. The risk isn't theoretical — it's already baked into live campaigns.

The corrective action isn't to slow AI adoption but to retrofit accountability mechanisms before regulators or brand crises force the issue. That means data-quality audits upstream of every AI decision, clear human-override triggers in automated workflows, and ownership of the governance question at the CMO level rather than leaving it to IT. The brands treating this as optional are the ones most exposed.

themes.head: Measurement's Credibility Crisis Deepens
body: Two sharp pieces this month argue that the measurement problem in marketing is not a tooling gap — it's a behavior gap. Marketers cherry-pick metrics that flatter campaigns, resist experimental designs that could disprove their assumptions, and mistake correlation for causation at scale. The result is that even sophisticated attribution platforms return garbage because the inputs and incentives are wrong.

The prescription — rigorous incrementality testing, holdout groups, and honest reporting upward — is well understood but politically uncomfortable. OpenAI's bold ad-revenue projections add a new wrinkle: as AI platforms enter the advertising market with their own measurement claims, brands will face competing, incompatible attribution narratives that make the existing confusion look manageable by comparison.
ev: MarTech · only way to know what ads did

themes.head: The Hidden ROI Tax on AI Adoption
body: As AI tooling proliferates — the 'sixteenth tool in a fifteen-tool stack' framing from Ai4 is a perfect snapshot — the real cost of AI is increasingly invisible in standard P&L reporting. Prompt engineering time, model fine-tuning, data cleaning, integration maintenance, and human review loops rarely appear in the line item labeled 'AI spend,' so ROI calculations systematically overstate returns.

The IFPA case study of running a global digital experience with two people shows the upside is real, but it depends on ruthless prioritization and treating hidden labor costs as first-class variables in any build-vs-buy decision. Organizations that don't surface these costs now will face a reckoning when budgets tighten and AI initiatives can't demonstrate auditable returns against full-cost baselines.
ev: Agile Brand · sixteenth tool in stack
Agile Brand · IFPA two-person global DX

month.takeaway: Across every story this month, the real stakes are not which AI tools to adopt but whether organizations have the governance, measurement honesty, and full-cost accounting to make AI adoption actually pay off.
